citations.assessment: Rav Naḥman explicitly remembers his father having been one of Shemuel’s judicial scribes. The passage leaves his patronymic unstated.
Tosafot explicitly says the unqualified name usually refers to Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov and explains its disagreement with the implication of Rashi’s gloss.
Heilprin’s Rav Naḥman dossier compares the same bare-name passage and reports this same identification.
Rashi explains the son-in-law remark in the mouth of Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak. Tosafot draws and rejects the more general identification. This also grounds Heilprin’s count of two views.
